summary: Latvia’s 2030 LULUCF balance target is −639 kt CO2eq within an EU-wide net-removals framework. The collective 2030 carbon-sink target is −310 Mt CO2-eq, also described as 310 Mt of net removals, with removals 42 Mt CO2-eq higher than the 2016–2018 average. Restoration is mainly an EU-level pledge: measures should cover at least 20% of EU land and sea areas by 2030—about 12,874 km² if the land share were applied proportionally to Latvia’s 64,370 km²—and all ecosystems needing restoration by 2050. EU-wide mitigation potentials are 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr from peatland and wetland rewetting and 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr from biodiversity-respecting reforestation and sustainable forest management. Improved fertiliser efficiency offers 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr. Latvia is 59.1% forest and 28.8% agricultural land, with grasslands and wetlands at 7.3% and 2.3%.
